newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Harriet and East Spar to share infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Harriet and East Spar to share infrastructure.

text.p: Apache Energy Ltd said on Monday the Harriet Joint Venture (HJV) and the East Spar Joint Venture (ESJV) had signed an agreement to share storage and transport infrastructure for their oil and gas fields offshore Western Australia.
"Under the agreement, the HJV will provide gas transportation and liquids storage services for the ESJV utilising existing Harriet oil and gas facilities," Apache said in a statement.
The HJV would benefit from increased utilisation of existing assets and receive additional revenue from service tariffs, Apache said.
It said the ESJV, in turn, would achieve lower full cycle project costs having eliminated major capital expenditures from their development such as the gas export pipeline and liquids storage tanks.

The location of the Harriet and East Spar gas processing facilities on Varanus Island has allowed the two joint ventures to share the infrastructure required to run and support the respective offshore gas developments, Apache said.
Apache said that in addition to operating the HJV's oil and gas facilities, provide operations services for the ESJV's facilities under a contract service arrangement.
"The cost of all operating resources and contract services such as supply boats and helicopters will be shared under the terms of the agreement," it said.

The Harriet Joint Venture partners are Apache, the operator, with 22.5 percent, Mobil Corp 25 percent, Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Corp 19.3 percent, Novus Petroleum Ltd 12.5 percent, Tap Oil NL 12.2 percent, Hardy Oil and Gas Plc 8.4 percent and New World Oil and
Participants in the East Spar Joint Venture are operator WMC Ltd with 30 percent, Mobil Corp 35 percent, Apache Corp 20 percent and Santos Ltd 15 percent.
